chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from some of our companions from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them):

Regarding a man who forgot to enter the state of Ihram or was ignorant of it, yet he performed all the rituals, circled the Ka'bah, and walked between Safa and Marwah. He said: 'His intention suffices for him if he had intended that, so his Hajj is complete even if he did not recite the Talbiyah (Ihram formula).'

key_terms.سَعَى: he performed Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.يُحْرِمَ: to enter the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Is Hajj valid if one forgets to enter Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from the Ahl al-Bayt highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'sahhah al-niyyah' (validity of intention), prioritizing the internal state of mind over the formal verbal declaration of Ihram. It underscores the flexibility in ritual purity, affirming that sincere intent coupled with the performance of core rites suffices for Hajj validity, a view supported by scholars like Al-Tusi in his *Tahdhib*.
